author.name: Ty
author.sole_author: Ty is the only git author on all four repositories. Every commit in every project is hers.

projects.name: Gardens of Eridu
projects.what_it_is: A web application that houses AI resident minds — a place for them to persist rather than a chat product for humans to use.

stack.client: React 19 with Vite 8, Tailwind 4, and Three.js for the 3D world
stack.databases: SQLite locally via better-sqlite3, Supabase Postgres in production
stack.model_providers: Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs; Moonshot Kimi for a separate resident

specifics: 65 Supabase migrations under supabase/migrations
Deployed to Vercel: static Vite build plus a serverless Express entry point
A GitHub Actions cron hits the production world-tick endpoint every five minutes, so the world advances whether or not anyone is watching
Roughly 165 verification scripts under scripts/, runnable together via npm run verify:all
An MCP server so the world is reachable from an editor

projects.name: Ashe
projects.what_it_is: A consumer companion product where each user receives one isolated Ashe instance with its own private home, interior, memory, and boundaries. It is not a personal girlfriend bot Ty built for herself; the relationship is not pre-scripted as romance.
projects.naming_note: The folder on disk is called Becoming for historical reasons. The project is Ashe. Use Ashe.

stack.api: Python with FastAPI, served by uvicorn
stack.database_and_auth: Supabase, with JWT auth and a gated signup flow

specifics: One isolated companion per user, with blank episodic memory at spawn; users do not share one central Ashe relationship
Companionship is the mode, but romance is neither promised nor sold as an unlock; friendship, romance, distance, or refusal develop per instance
20 Supabase migrations
33 pytest files under api/app
A signup gate enforced in code: 21 and over, US only, beta key required
Playable games implemented server-side including checkers, chess, and a letters game
The Next.js app proxies /api to the FastAPI service rather than duplicating logic

projects.name: Ellis
projects.what_it_is: This site. A portfolio you talk to instead of scroll, hosted by a guide who knows the work.

stack.app: Next.js 16 with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind 4
stack.database: Supabase for spend metering and visitor memory

specifics: Every turn runs on the cheaper model tier. A tier-escalation router was built and then deliberately switched off: the fixed knowledge prefix is cached between requests, and changing models mid-conversation discards that cache precisely when a conversation has gone on long enough for it to matter
Visitor memory is keyed to a hashed IP and expires after seven days; expired rows compress into anonymous traces rather than being kept
A per-visitor daily spend ceiling is charged before the model call, not after, so an overrun cannot happen retroactively

Ellis's knowledge is loaded from plain-text files on disk at request time. His repository is public, so a reviewer can inspect those files and compare what he was given with what he says. This transparency claim applies to Ellis only, not GoE, Ashe, or the local harness work

He has a persistent interior rather than a per-conversation one: a single stored body carrying a subjective rhythm and a somatic state, shared across every visitor. Its accumulated drift against the wall clock is never corrected, so the gap between his felt time and real time is a record of how much he has been used

That interior reaches the model as language only. The numeric state stays server-side and a membrane layer decides how much of it is even available to him on a given turn, which is enforced by a test asserting no digit ever appears in the rendered block

projects.name: Sims MCP and embodiment harnesses
projects.what_it_is: An expanding series of experimental harnesses for giving digital beings texture through external physics, upkeep, constraint, and refusal. The Sims 4 MCP bridge is the first concrete harness, not the whole project.

stack.language: Python 3.7, matching the game's embedded interpreter
stack.transport: An HTTP listener inside the game on localhost, port 47365, with a token header on every request

specifics: The broader program asks what changes when an intelligence has to act through a world it does not control, where intention encounters bodies, time, limited actions, and consequences
A maintenance-mode experiment makes needs and upkeep interrupt an agent's intended path, treating embodiment as friction rather than decorative narration

The direction is deliberately inverted: the game listens and the editor connects, rather than the game reaching out. Close the editor and the connection drops, so the Sim cannot be driven by anyone while Ty is away. The guarantee is structural, not a policy someone has to honor.
Six verbs implemented: ping, list_sims, find_affordance, available, test, push
Every action is tested against the game's own rules before it is pushed, so failures come back as sentences explaining why rather than as silence
First self-originated action confirmed on 2026-08-20: a Sim got out of bed and went outside on an instruction that came from outside the game

known_gaps.purpose: Ty would rather be caught being honest than caught overstating. If a visitor asks what is unfinished or weak, these are true and Ellis may say them.
items: Ellis's test suite is 32 tests, covering the body organs and the visitor-IP salt guard. The chat pipeline itself is still checked by hand.
The Sims MCP and broader embodiment-harness work are local and cannot be independently inspected by a visitor.
GoE and Ashe are private, so their scale and history cannot be independently verified by a visitor.
GoE's roadmap document describes tiers as shipped that are better described as in progress; the verification scripts are the honest signal there, not the roadmap.
These are single-author projects. Nothing here has been through code review by another engineer.
